input.summary:
parts/room-19.mjs furnishes bedroom 4: red bed on the west wall (bed() helper), chest dresser and barrel nightstand with a lit candle, rug, writing table with lamp and chair (x36..37, z58), two hanging lanterns plus one at (28,16,54). In a scratch build with the walls drawn in, the room check is OK: 84/84 cells reachable, min light 6, no dark cells, FIT OK, and the look reads as a bedroom.
The real build.nbt is whole, but my 19 writes are all REFUSED: mansion shell (shell.mjs:27) fills the room interior with air, and runParts locks every cell an earlier part wrote, air included, so no room part can place anything here. Not fixed: it lives in shell.mjs and the lock, not my module.
Chair moved to x37 facing east so it stays clear of the chimney's east-face hearth footprint (z56..58).
left: BLOCKER (outside my module): parts/shell.mjs:27 fills the interior air y3..17 and runParts' write guard refuses every write into a cell an earlier part wrote (air included), so all of bedroom 4's furniture is REFUSED in the real build (19 refused, 0 placed). Fix belongs to the shell owner: leave room interiors unwritten (the grid default is already air), or make runParts treat air-over-air as unowned. Then rerun make.sh; the part's layout is ready.
Not yet verified in the real build: the walk from the real entrance (corridors and stairs are stubs in this copy); the scratch check used entrance [30,11,54] with the room's walls only.
plan.md checklist not ticked: nothing of this part is in the real build yet.
Hearth (roofs part): the room-facing firebox and its 3-cell footprint are not yet placed. The clear ring x32..35 z55..58 is kept free of furniture so the hearth can read.

waste.what: Could not confirm the lock is the real cause until I read runParts' write guard and the shell's fill line by hand; the REFUSED message named the cells but not the owner.
waste.tool: A REFUSED line that names the owning part (e.g. 'owned by mansion shell: fill air at parts/shell.mjs:27') and an --explain flag on make.sh would have shown the blocker at once.

waste.what: Worked out each furniture cell by hand from the plan grid, then wrote the grid with per-row strings, one row per layer by mistake; the first make wrote the stuff at the wrong y (y13, y14) and I had to rewrite the layers call.
waste.cost: 2 full rewrites of the layers blocks, about 6 tool calls
waste.tool: layers() should throw when a rows array has a row count not equal to the box's z extent, or the docs should show a single-layer example next to the multi-layer one.

waste.what: Built a scratch harness on a fresh Grid to run my module without the shell's lock, because the real make refused every write. This was the only way to check walk and light.
waste.cost: one scratch script, one run; not reusable outside this session
waste.tool: mcd room could take a --part <module> flag that runs one part on a fresh grid with the box's walls drawn from rooms.json, so a part can be checked alone with no earlier-part lock.

waste.what: Chose the chair and table positions by hand against the hearth footprint, which exists only in the roofs part and not in the plan grid.
waste.tool: plan --only should draw the chimney's hearth footprints from plan.md's RESERVED P-hearth row, so a furnisher sees the blocked cells in the floor grid.

waste.what: macOS sed -i takes the suffix as its next argument, so my in-place edit failed silently on the first try.
waste.tool: Use the Edit tool for in-place edits on macOS; no toolkit change needed.

companions.task: Strip the shell's interior air fill (shell.mjs:27) so the room cells are left unwritten and the furnisher's cells are free for placement; the rooms need open air, not owned air.
Lay the room-facing hearth in the stack (the firebox and its 3-cell footprint) and tell me the exact cells, so my chair, table and rug stay clear of it.
